correctness.summary: For normal A, the squared Rayleigh residual is the spectral variance under weights |c_i|^2. Filtering and normalization reweight these probabilities by |phi(lambda_i)|^2. The variance-minimization identity gives the state-dependent m/s and M/s bounds, and a two-eigenvalue family proves the global M/m and m/M constants sharp. The zero-gain construction and single-eigenspace exception exhaust the singular cases. The separation minimax result follows from M>=alpha and m<=beta and is attained by two-level gain filters.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Checked classical normal inverse-iteration residual theory, Chebyshev-Davidson, polynomial-filtered Lanczos, least-squares rational filtering, filtered-subspace convergence/discretization theory, recent residual-based Chebyshev filtered subspace iteration, and 2026 work on conditioning of Chebyshev-filtered vector blocks. These sources cover fixed-shift residual monotonicity, spectral-gain separation, eigenspace convergence, filter design, inexact products, and block-vector conditioning. Searches did not locate the exact one-vector Rayleigh-residual M/m distortion law, its zero-gain classification, or the sharp 1/eta separation-versus-residual minimax tradeoff. The elementary variance-comparison proof means older spectral-transformation, simultaneous-iteration, or probability literature remains a meaningful historical-equivalence risk.

value.summary: The result identifies an exact diagnostic cost of spectral selectivity: the same wanted/unwanted gain contrast that accelerates filtered eigenspace convergence forces worst-case raw Rayleigh-residual spikes. The reciprocal minimax law is sharp, the zero-gain endpoint is classified, and power/inverse-iteration corollaries make the effect concrete. This separates pure-filter residual behavior from Rayleigh-Ritz-extracted residual behavior and gives a precise caution for residual-based stopping diagnostics during filtering.

limitations: Exact arithmetic, finite-dimensional normal matrices, exact filter application, and Euclidean Rayleigh residual for the main theorem.
Nonnormal matrices, roundoff, inexact shifted solves, and approximate filter evaluation are outside scope.
A complete filtered eigensolver includes orthogonalization and Rayleigh-Ritz extraction; its post-extraction residuals are not claimed to satisfy the pure-filter one-step law.
Unbounded relative amplification occurs as the input residual tends to zero and does not imply unbounded absolute residuals or algorithmic divergence.
The minimax separation result does not constrain polynomial degree, rational poles, sparsity, or evaluation cost.
Older spectral-transformation, simultaneous-iteration, and general variance-comparison literature was not exhaustively inspected theorem by theorem, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
